sub_scenario.one_line: product accessibility lead: conditional on delaying the hot-desk start

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the screen-reader remediation brief and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The engineering hot desks review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I prepared the keyboard-navigation remediation brief in the accessibility lab while replaying the screen-reader recordings.
What did the lab provide?
I could trace each failure from the recording to a specific component.
Someone new shadowed me in the Tuesday release review this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the accessibility lab into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
At an engineering hot desk, notification banners and pair-programming requests interrupted a remediation brief.
What was the consequence?
I matched two defects to the wrong components and delayed the fix.
I can answer design questions from the engineering hot desks during stand-up.
Are those questions manageable?
Yes, when I am addressing one interface decision.
I archived last cycle's notes on the engineering hot desks and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The accessibility lab has a test device available after 13:00, but the release review is at 15:00 and the hot-desk shift starts at 14:00.
Is there a workable arrangement?
Yes, if the shift begins after I finish the device review.
A vendor call about the screen-reader remediation brief ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the Tuesday release review checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the accessibility lab.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the engineering hot desks records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
During the last mobile release, a stream of hot-desk requests interrupted my replay of the screen-reader sessions and I linked two focus failures to the wrong controls.
How was that resolved?
The engineering team lost a day retesting the components.
I sketched next week's plan for the accessibility lab before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the screen-reader remediation brief updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The release manager needs the tested brief in the review folder by 14:45, before the 15:00 meeting.
Can the test session be shortened?
No, each recording has to be replayed on the reserved device.
I compared two options for the engineering hot desks tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the Tuesday release review handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Why should my engineering hot-desk shift depend on finishing the accessibility-lab review first?
